# laravelforge_security_rules (Resource)

Add a new security rule to the site.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravelforge_security_rules" "example" {
  credentials = [{
    username = "deploy"
    password = "secret"
  }]
  name         = "Restricted Access"
  organization = "my-org"
  server       = 123456
  site         = 123456
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `credentials` (Attributes List, Sensitive) The credentials for the security rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `name` (String) The name of the security rule.
- `organization` (String) The organization slug
- `server` (Number) The server ID
- `site` (Number) The site ID

### Optional

- `path` (String) The path for the security rule.
- `security_rule` (Number) The security rule ID

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The date and time the security rule was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `status` (String) The status of the security rule.
- `updated_at` (String) The date and time the security rule was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `password` (String) The passwords for the credential.
- `username` (String) The usernames for the credential.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import laravelforge_security_rules.example my-org/123456/123456/123
```
